title: Weekly Markets Monitor - Chill and boom
gist: WGC's weekly monitor argues the sharp fall in Treasury yields and the collapse in Fed hike odds (from ~70% to under 10%) reflect a rotation out of weak AI stocks, not easing inflation. Thursday's PCE (3.6% expected) and Q3 GDP (3.2%) could reverse the bond-over-gold preference.

insights.claim: Last week Middle East tensions pushed oil to a six-month high while concerns over AI spending weighed on technology stocks, keeping geopolitical and market risk elevated.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Oil and AI-capex worries are the two live risk drivers into the Fed meeting.

insights.claim: US Treasury yields fell sharply and the dollar softened last week while global equities ended mixed, alongside resilient US activity and China Q3 growth beating expectations.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Falling yields with a resilient US economy is an unusual mix that hinges on the rotation story.

insights.claim: Euro-area business activity softened amid social unrest and Japan saw higher inflation.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Regional divergence: euro-area growth risk versus Japanese inflation pressure.

themes.theme: Fed repricing and the bond rotation

insights.claim: Market-implied probability of another Fed rate hike at the Wednesday FOMC meeting has fallen to under 10%, from around 70% a month ago.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: A hike is almost fully priced out, so upside inflation data is the main source of repricing risk.

insights.claim: The decline in Treasury yields reflects a rotation into bonds amid weakness in AI-related stocks rather than a meaningful softening in inflation expectations.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: If the yield drop is a flight-to-safety flow rather than disinflation, it can reverse quickly.
insights.quote: In our view, the recent decline in bond yields reflects a rotation into Treasuries amid weakness in AI-related stocks, rather than a meaningful softening in inflation expectations.

insights.claim: Markets are vulnerable to Thursday's PCE inflation print, expected to accelerate to 3.6% y/y.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: A hot PCE print against a priced-out Fed would hit bonds and force Fed repricing.
insights.quote: That leaves markets vulnerable to Thursday's PCE inflation print

insights.claim: Expected Q3 US GDP growth rising from 2.2% to 3.2% could complicate the Fed repricing, temper the bond rotation and call into question the recent apparent preference for bonds over gold.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: The author frames strong data as a catalyst for flows to swing back from Treasuries toward gold.
insights.quote: call into question the recent apparent preference for bonds over gold

insights.claim: The recent apparent preference of investors for bonds over gold is framed as a temporary, rotation-driven phenomenon that strong data could unwind.
insights.speaker: @goldcouncil
insights.so_what: Gold dips tied to bond-rotation flows may be buyable if inflation data surprises upward.
